source.title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals

accepted.question_text: For a set of reals X, let O be the family of open covers of X, Ω the family of open ω-covers (every finite subset of X is contained in some member), and Γ the family of open γ-covers (infinite covers in which each point belongs to all but finitely many members). The property Sfin(A,B) means that from each cover in a sequence from A one can choose finitely many members so that the union of all chosen members is a cover in B; Ufin(A,B) is the analogous finite-selection property for sequences of covers with no finite subcover, where the sequence of finite unions belongs to B. Is the property Ufin(O, Ω) exactly the same as Sfin(Γ, Ω)? If they are different, does Ufin(O, Γ) at least imply Sfin(Γ, Ω)?

evidence.quote: (1) Is Ufin(O, Ω) = Sfin(Γ, Ω)? (2) And if not, does Ufin(O, Γ) imply Sfin(Γ, Ω)?

accepted.question_text: For a set of reals X, let O be the family of open covers of X, Ω the family of open ω-covers (every finite subset of X is contained in some member), and Γ the family of open γ-covers (infinite covers in which each point belongs to all but finitely many members). The property Sfin(A,B) means that from each cover in a sequence from A one can choose finitely many members so that the union of all chosen members is a cover in B; Ufin(A,B) is the analogous finite-selection property for sequences of covers with no finite subcover, where the sequence of finite unions belongs to B. Can a Borel subgroup of a Polish group that is not σ-compact be generated by a subspace whose open covers satisfy Ufin(O, Γ)?

evidence.quote: Can a Borel non-σ-compact subgroup of a Polish group be generated by a subspace satisfying Ufin(O, Γ)?

accepted.question_text: For a set of reals X, let O be the family of open covers of X, Ω the family of open ω-covers (every finite subset of X is contained in some member), and Γ the family of open γ-covers (infinite covers in which each point belongs to all but finitely many members). The property Sfin(A,B) means that from each cover in a sequence from A one can choose finitely many members so that the union of all chosen members is a cover in B; Ufin(A,B) is the analogous finite-selection property for sequences of covers with no finite subcover, where the sequence of finite unions belongs to B. Suppose X is a subset of a Borel set B ⊆ R and X satisfies Ufin(O, Γ). Must there exist a σ-compact set F with X ⊂ F ⊂ B? Is the answer still yes when B is an Fσδ set?

evidence.quote: Assume that X ⊆ B ⊆ R, B is Borel, and X satisfies Ufin(O, Γ). Must there be a σ-compact F with X ⊂ F ⊂ B? What if B is Fσδ?

accepted.question_text: Let S1(Γ, Γ) mean that for every sequence of open γ-covers of a set of reals X one can choose one member from each cover and still obtain a γ-cover. Does ZFC prove the existence of a set of reals X with S1(Γ, Γ) and cardinality b?

evidence.quote: Does there exist (in ZFC) a set of reals X satisfying S1(Γ, Γ) such that |X| = b?

accepted.question_text: Let Sfin(Ω, Ω) mean that for every sequence of open ω-covers of a set of reals X one can choose finitely many members from each cover so that all chosen sets together still form an open ω-cover. Does ZFC prove the existence of a set of reals with Sfin(Ω, Ω) and cardinality d?

evidence.quote: Does there exist (in ZFC) a set of reals satisfying Sfin(Ω, Ω) such that |X| = d?

accepted.question_text: For a set of reals X, let O be the family of open covers of X, Ω the family of open ω-covers (every finite subset of X is contained in some member), and Γ the family of open γ-covers (infinite covers in which each point belongs to all but finitely many members). The property Sfin(A,B) means that from each cover in a sequence from A one can choose finitely many members so that the union of all chosen members is a cover in B; Ufin(A,B) is the analogous finite-selection property for sequences of covers with no finite subcover, where the sequence of finite unions belongs to B. Is there a direct, non-dichotomic construction of a set of reals M that satisfies Sfin(Ω, Ω) but fails Ufin(O, Γ)?

evidence.quote: Is there a direct (non-dichotomic) construction of a set of reals M satisfying Sfin(Ω, Ω) but not Ufin(O, Γ)?

accepted.question_text: Let B denote the family of countable Borel covers of a set of reals. Borel’s Conjecture for a class J means that every member of J is countable. Is it consistent that every set of reals satisfying Sfin(B, B) is countable?

evidence.quote: Is Borel’s Conjecture for Sfin(B, B) consistent?

accepted.question_text: Is the statement that every set of reals satisfying Sfin(B, B) is countable equivalent to the statement that every set of reals satisfying S1(BΓ, BΩ) is countable, where BΩ and BΓ are the countable Borel ω-covers and γ-covers?

evidence.quote: Is Borel’s Conjecture for Sfin(B, B) equivalent to Borel’s Conjecture for S1(BΓ, BΩ)?

accepted.question_text: Let BΩ be the family of countable Borel ω-covers. Is it consistent that every set of reals satisfying Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) is countable?

evidence.quote: Is Borel’s Conjecture for Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) consistent?

accepted.question_text: Does Martin’s Axiom imply that there exists a set of reals of size continuum such that every sequence of countable Borel ω-covers admits single selections forming a Borel γ-cover, i.e. the set satisfies S1(BΩ, BΓ)?

evidence.quote: Does Martin’s Axiom imply the existence of a set of reals of cardinality continuum, satisfying S1(BΩ, BΓ)?

accepted.question_text: For a set of reals X, the δ-property means that for every open ω-cover U of X, the space X belongs to the closure of U under the lim inf operation. The property (Ω over Γ) means that every open ω-cover of X contains an open γ-subcover. Are these two properties equivalent?

evidence.quote: Is the δ-property equivalent to (Ω Γ)?

accepted.question_text: If each member of an increasing sequence X0 ⊆ X1 ⊆ ··· of sets of reals has the property that every open ω-cover contains an open γ-subcover, must the union ⋃n Xn have the same property?

evidence.quote: Does every union of an increasing sequence {Xn}n∈N of sets satisfying (Ω Γ) satisfy (Ω Γ)?

accepted.question_text: For sets of reals, is either of the Borel selection properties S1(BΩ, BΩ) or Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) hereditary, meaning inherited by every subset?

evidence.quote: Is S1(BΩ, BΩ) or Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) hereditary?

accepted.question_text: If a set of reals X satisfies Sfin(Γ, Ω) or S1(Γ, Ω), must every Fσ subset of X satisfy the same respective property?

evidence.quote: Are Sfin(Γ, Ω) and S1(Γ, Ω) hereditary for Fσ subsets?

accepted.question_text: If a set of reals X satisfies S1(BΩ, BΩ) or Sfin(BΩ, BΩ), must every finite power X^k satisfy the same property?

evidence.quote: Are any of the classes S1(BΩ, BΩ) or Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) preserved by finite powers?

accepted.question_text: If a set of reals X satisfies S1(BΩ, BΓ), must every finite power X^k also satisfy S1(BΩ, BΓ)?

evidence.quote: Is S1(BΩ, BΓ) preserved by finite powers?

accepted.question_text: For a set of reals X, let O be the family of open covers of X, Ω the family of open ω-covers (every finite subset of X is contained in some member), and Γ the family of open γ-covers (infinite covers in which each point belongs to all but finitely many members). The property Sfin(A,B) means that from each cover in a sequence from A one can choose finitely many members so that the union of all chosen members is a cover in B; Ufin(A,B) is the analogous finite-selection property for sequences of covers with no finite subcover, where the sequence of finite unions belongs to B. Suppose X and Y each satisfy S1(O, O), and X additionally satisfies Ufin(O, Γ). Must the product X × Y also satisfy S1(O, O)?

evidence.quote: Assume that X, Y ⊆ R satisfy S1(O, O), and X also satisfies Ufin(O, Γ). Does it follow that X × Y satisfies S1(O, O)?

accepted.question_text: For a set of reals X, let O be the family of open covers of X, Ω the family of open ω-covers (every finite subset of X is contained in some member), and Γ the family of open γ-covers (infinite covers in which each point belongs to all but finitely many members). The property Sfin(A,B) means that from each cover in a sequence from A one can choose finitely many members so that the union of all chosen members is a cover in B; Ufin(A,B) is the analogous finite-selection property for sequences of covers with no finite subcover, where the sequence of finite unions belongs to B. Is the class of sets of reals that satisfy both Ufin(O, Γ) and S1(O, O) closed under finite products?

evidence.quote: Is Ufin(O, Γ) ∩ S1(O, O) preserved by finite products?

accepted.question_text: For the Sfin- and Ufin-type covering properties appearing in the Scheepers diagram, is there a model of set theory in which at least one of these properties is preserved under finite products?

evidence.quote: Are any of the Sfin or Ufin type properties in the Scheepers diagram 1 consistently preserved by finite products?

accepted.question_text: If X is a set of reals of cardinality less than p and Y is a set of Hausdorff dimension zero, must the product X × Y also have Hausdorff dimension zero?

evidence.quote: Assume that |X| < p. Is it true that for each Y with Hausdorff dimension zero, X × Y has Hausdorff dimension zero?

accepted.question_text: Is there a model of ZFC containing uncountable sets of reals with S1(Ω, Γ) such that nevertheless, for every such set X and every Hausdorff-dimension-zero set Y, the product X × Y still has Hausdorff dimension zero?

evidence.quote: Is it consistent (relative to ZFC) that there are uncountable sets of reals satisfying S1(Ω, Γ), but for each such set X and each set Y with Hausdorff dimension zero, X × Y has Hausdorff dimension zero?

accepted.question_text: Is there a model of set theory in which the covering property Sfin(Ω, Ω) is additive, i.e. preserved under finite unions?

evidence.quote: Is Sfin(Ω, Ω) consistently additive?

accepted.question_text: Is there a model of set theory in which the Borel property Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) is additive?

evidence.quote: Is Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) consistently additive?

accepted.question_text: Is the additivity number of the Menger property Sfin(O, O) exactly max{b, g}?

evidence.quote: Is add(Sfin(O, O)) = max{b, g}?

accepted.question_text: Is the additivity number of the γ-property S1(Γ, Γ) equal to b?

evidence.quote: Is add(S1(Γ, Γ)) = b?

accepted.question_text: Is it consistent that the additivity number of the null ideal N is strictly smaller than the additivity number of S1(O, O)?

evidence.quote: Is it consistent that add(N) < add(S1(O, O))?

accepted.question_text: If X has the γ-property S1(Ω, Γ) and D is a set of reals of size less than p, must X ∪ D still satisfy S1(Ω, Γ)? Under Martin’s Axiom, must this remain true when |D| = ℵ1?

evidence.quote: Assume that X satisfies S1(Ω, Γ) and |D| < p. Does X ∪ D satisfy S1(Ω, Γ)? Is it true under Martin’s Axiom when |D| = ℵ1?

accepted.question_text: Let T be the family of open τ-covers, where an open cover is a τ-cover if each point lies in infinitely many members and, for each two points x and y, one of the two asymmetric difference families is finite. Is the property that every open ω-cover contains a γ-subcover equivalent to the property that every open ω-cover contains a τ-subcover?

evidence.quote: Is (Ω Γ) = (Ω T)?

accepted.question_text: Is the property that every open ω-cover contains an open τ-subcover equivalent to the finite-selection property Sfin(Ω, T)?

evidence.quote: Is (Ω T) = Sfin(Ω, T)?

accepted.question_text: If a set of reals satisfies S1(Ω, T), meaning that one can choose a single set from each open ω-cover in a sequence so that the chosen family is a τ-cover, must it also satisfy Ufin(O, Γ)?

evidence.quote: Does S1(Ω, T) imply Ufin(O, Γ)?

accepted.question_text: Are any of the Borel τ-cover properties S1(BT, BΓ), S1(BT, BT), S1(BT, BΩ), S1(BT, B), Sfin(BT, BT), or Sfin(BT, BΩ) inherited by all subsets?

evidence.quote: Are any of the properties S1(BT, BΓ), S1(BT, BT), S1(BT, BΩ), S1(BT, B), Sfin(BT, BT), or Sfin(BT, BΩ), hereditary?

accepted.question_text: Are any of the τ-cover selection properties S1(T, T), Sfin(T, T), S1(Γ, T), Sfin(Γ, T), or Ufin(O, T), or any of their Borel analogues, additive under finite unions?

evidence.quote: Are any of the properties S1(T, T), Sfin(T, T), S1(Γ, T), Sfin(Γ, T), and Ufin(O, T) (or any of their Borel versions) additive?

accepted.question_text: Are any of the τ-cover selection properties S1(Ω, T), Sfin(Ω, T), S1(T, Γ), S1(T, T), S1(T, Ω), Sfin(T, T), or Sfin(T, Ω) preserved under finite powers?

evidence.quote: Are any of the properties (1) S1(Ω, T), or Sfin(Ω, T), (2) S1(T, Γ), S1(T, T), S1(T, Ω), Sfin(T, T), or Sfin(T, Ω), preserved under taking finite powers?

accepted.question_text: Let T* be the family of countable open τ*-covers, where a cover U = {Un : n ∈ N} is a τ*-cover if it is large and the family of index sets {n : x ∈ Un}, x ∈ X, is linearly refinable modulo finite sets. Does the Cantor space {0,1}^N satisfy the property that every open τ*-cover contains a γ-subcover?

evidence.quote: Does {0, 1}N satisfy (T* Γ)?

accepted.question_text: Let ג(T) denote the family of T-glueable covers: covers that are either multifinite or can be partitioned into finite blocks whose unions form an open τ-cover. Is Ufin(O, T) equivalent to Sfin(Ω, ג(T))?

evidence.quote: Is Ufin(O, T) = Sfin(Ω, ג(T))?

accepted.question_text: Let ג(Ω) be the family of Ω-glueable covers obtained from the Gimel operator. Is the classical property S1(Ω, Ω) equivalent to S1(Ω, ג(Ω))?

evidence.quote: Is S1(Ω, Ω) = S1(Ω, ג(Ω))?

accepted.question_text: Let Λ denote the family of large open covers and let ג(Ω) be the family of Ω-glueable covers. Is the property Ufin(O, Ω) equivalent to the statement that every large open cover contains an Ω-glueable subcover?

evidence.quote: Is Ufin(O, Ω) = (Λ ג(Ω))?

accepted.question_text: For collections of covers A and B, Split(A, B) means that every cover in A can be partitioned into two disjoint subfamilies each containing a member of B. Does Split(Ω, T) imply Split(T, Γ)? If not, does Split(Ω, T) at least imply Split(Λ, Λ)?

evidence.quote: (1) Does Split(Ω, T) imply Split(T, Γ)? (2) And if not, then does Split(Ω, T) imply Split(Λ, Λ)?

accepted.question_text: If X is compact and Y has the property that every large open cover of Y can be split into two disjoint large subcovers, must the product X × Y also have Split(Λ, Λ)?

evidence.quote: Assume that X is compact and Y satisfies Split(Λ, Λ). Does X × Y satisfy Split(Λ, Λ)?

accepted.question_text: Can one improve either the lower bound or the upper bound in the inequality ℵ1 ≤ add(Split(Ω, Λ)) ≤ c for the additivity number of Split(Ω, Λ)?

evidence.quote: Improve the lower bound or the upper bound in the inequality ℵ1 ≤ add(Split(Ω, Λ)) ≤ c.

accepted.question_text: Can the known lower bound u for the additivity number add(Split(T, T)) be strengthened?

evidence.quote: Can the lower bound u on add(Split(T, T)) be improved?

accepted.question_text: Is the splitting property Split(Λ, Λ) additive under finite unions?

evidence.quote: Is Split(Λ, Λ) additive?

accepted.question_text: Are any of the Borel splitting properties Split(BΩ, BΛ), Split(BΩ, BΩ), Split(BT, BT), or Split(BT, BΓ) hereditary?

evidence.quote: Are any of the properties Split(BΩ, BΛ), Split(BΩ, BΩ), Split(BT, BT), and Split(BT, BΓ) hereditary?

accepted.question_text: Are any of the splitting properties Split(Ω, Ω), Split(Ω, T), or Split(T, T) preserved by finite powers?

evidence.quote: Are any of the properties Split(Ω, Ω), Split(Ω, T), or Split(T, T) preserved under taking finite powers?

accepted.question_text: Let Cp(X) be the space of continuous real-valued functions on X with the topology of pointwise convergence, and let Γ0 denote the countably infinite subsets converging to the zero function. If κ < b and each Cp(Xα) satisfies S1(Γ0, Γ0), must Cp(⋃α<κ Xα) also satisfy S1(Γ0, Γ0)?

evidence.quote: Assume that κ < b, and for each α < λ, Cp(Xα) satisfies S1(Γ0, Γ0). Does Cp(⋃α<κ Xα) satisfy S1(Γ0, Γ0)?

accepted.question_text: Is the function-space property S1(Γ0, Γ0) of Cp(X) equivalent to the covering property S1(Γ, Γ) of the underlying set of reals X?

evidence.quote: Is S1(Γ0, Γ0) for Cp(X) equivalent to S1(Γ, Γ) for X?

accepted.question_text: Is the function-space property S1(Γ0, Ω0) of Cp(X) equivalent to the covering property S1(Γ, Ω) of X?

evidence.quote: Is S1(Γ0, Ω0) for Cp(X) equivalent to S1(Γ, Ω) for X?

accepted.question_text: Let O(Ωx) be the family of open subsets of a space that accumulate at x, and Γx the countably infinite sets converging to x. What is the least cardinality of a set X ⊆ R for which Cp(X) fails the property that every member of O(Ωx) contains a subset in Γx, for each x?

evidence.quote: What is the minimal cardinality of a set X ⊆ R such that Cp(X) does not satisfy (O(Ωx) Γx)?

accepted.question_text: For a topological group G, let Onbd denote the covers {g·U : g ∈ G} arising from neighborhoods U of the identity. Are there, in ZFC, groups G and H that satisfy Sfin(Onbd, O) even though G × H does not?

evidence.quote: Are there, in ZFC, groups G, H satisfying Sfin(Onbd, O) such that G × H does not satisfy Sfin(Onbd, O)?

accepted.question_text: Let Ωnbd be the covers {F·U : F is finite, U is an identity neighborhood, and F·U ≠ G}. For separable metrizable groups, is S1(Ωnbd, Ω) equal to Sfin(Onbd, O)? More specifically, does the Continuum Hypothesis produce a counterexample, and is it consistent that the two properties coincide?

evidence.quote: Is S1(Ωnbd, Ω) = Sfin(Onbd, O) for separable metrizable groups? Specifically: (1) Does the Continuum Hypothesis imply the existence of a separable metrizable group G satisfying Sfin(Onbd, O) but not S1(Ωnbd, Ω)? (2) Is it consistent that Sfin(Onbd, O) = S1(Ωnbd, Ω) for separable metrizable groups?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an analytic topological group that satisfies Sfin(Onbd, O) but fails S1(Ωnbd, Γ)?

evidence.quote: Is there an analytic group satisfying Sfin(Onbd, O) but not S1(Ωnbd, Γ)?

accepted.question_text: Is it consistent that there exists a subgroup G ≤ Z^N with strong measure zero that is unbounded with respect to eventual domination and does not satisfy Sfin(O, O)?

evidence.quote: Is it consistent that there is G ≤ ZN such that G has strong measure zero, is unbounded, and does not satisfy Sfin(O, O)?

accepted.question_text: Is it consistent that there exists a subgroup G ≤ Z^N having strong measure zero and satisfying Sfin(O, O), while still being unbounded and failing S1(O, O)?

evidence.quote: Is it consistent that there is G ≤ ZN such that G has strong measure zero and satisfies Sfin(O, O), but is unbounded and does not satisfy S1(O, O)?

accepted.question_text: Does ZFC prove the existence of a subgroup G ≤ Z^N of cardinality d satisfying Sfin(O, O)?

evidence.quote: Is there (in ZFC) a group G ≤ ZN of cardinality d satisfying Sfin(O, O)?

accepted.question_text: Does the Continuum Hypothesis imply that there exists a subgroup G ≤ Z^N of size c satisfying the Borel γ-property S1(BΩ, BΓ), or at least the open-cover γ-property S1(Ω, Γ)?

evidence.quote: Does the Continuum Hypothesis imply the existence of a group G ≤ ZN of cardinality c satisfying S1(BΩ, BΓ), or at least S1(Ω, Γ)?

accepted.question_text: Is it consistent that the pseudointersection number p is strictly less than the tower number t?

evidence.quote: Is it consistent that p < t?

accepted.question_text: Let p* be the minimal size of a centered family of infinite subsets of N that is not linearly refinable modulo finite sets. Is p equal to p*?

evidence.quote: Is p = p*?

accepted.question_text: Let od be the minimal cardinality of a τ-family that is not o-diagonalizable. Is it consistent that cov(M), the covering number of the meager ideal, is strictly smaller than od?

evidence.quote: Is it consistent that cov(M) < od?

accepted.question_text: For κ > 1, let pκ be the minimal size of a centered family in [N]^{ℵ0} that cannot be partitioned into fewer than κ subfamilies each with a pseudo-intersection. Is p_p equal to t?

evidence.quote: Is pp = t?

accepted.question_text: Let add(X, D) be the Ramsey-theoretic cardinal defined in the paper using the “avoids middles” relation on dominating families in N^N. Must cov(M) be at most add(X, D)?

evidence.quote: Is cov(M) ≤ add(X, D)?

accepted.question_text: If X satisfies Ufin(O, Ω) and Y is a continuous image of X in N^N, let G be the set of functions eventually dominated by the pointwise maximum of some finite subset of Y. Must G also satisfy Ufin(O, Ω)?

evidence.quote: Assume that X satisfies Ufin(O, Ω). Does it follow that G = {g ∈ NN : (∃k)(∃f1, . . . , fk ∈ Y ) g ≤* max{f1, . . . , fk}} satisfies Ufin(O, Ω)?

accepted.question_text: If every subset Y of X is concentrated on some countable subset of Y, must X be a continuous image of a ν-set?

evidence.quote: Assume that X ⊆ R, and for each Y ⊆ X, Y is concentrated on a countable subset of Y. Does it follow that X is a continuous image of a ν-set?

accepted.question_text: Is it consistent that cov(M) = ℵ1, the continuum c equals ℵω1, and there exists a Luzin set of size c?

evidence.quote: Is it consistent that cov(M) = ℵ1 < c = ℵω1, and there is a c-Luzin set?

accepted.question_text: If every strong measure zero set of reals is meager-additive, must Borel’s Conjecture follow?
accepted.context_brief: strong measure zero versus Borel conjecture

evidence.quote: Assume that every strong measure zero set of reals is meager-additive. Does Borel’s Conjecture follow?

accepted.question_text: If X and Y are meager-additive subsets of R, must X × Y be meager-additive? Likewise, if X and Y are null-additive, must X × Y be null-additive?

evidence.quote: Assume that X, Y ⊆ R are meager- (respectively, null-) additive. Does it follow that X × Y is meager- (respectively, null-) additive?

accepted.question_text: If X ⊆ [0,1] is meager-additive or null-additive as a subset of R, must it remain meager-additive or null-additive when identified with a subset of the Cantor space {0,1}^N?
accepted.context_brief: transfer between R and Cantor space

evidence.quote: Assume that X ⊆ R is meager- (respectively, null-) additive, and X ⊆ [0, 1]. Does it follow that X is meager- (respectively, null-) additive when viewed as a subset of {0, 1}N?

accepted.question_text: If X ⊆ N^N is nonmeager and Y ⊆ N^N is dominating, does there exist a Borel set H ⊆ N^N × N^N such that every meager subset of N^N is contained in the vertical section Hx for some x in X ∪ Y?

evidence.quote: Assume that X ⊆ NN is nonmeager and Y ⊆ NN is dominating. Is there a Borel set H ⊆ NN × NN such that every meager set is contained in Hx for some x ∈ X ∪ Y?

needs_review.question_text_raw: Does the Continuum Hypothesis imply a realization of the settings (d),(e),(g),(j), and (l)?

evidence.quote: Does the Continuum Hypothesis imply a realization of the settings (d),(e),(g),(j), and (l)?
